A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same representation-shattering study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material across appendix reorganization.

before.justification: V2 reports original synthetic Transformer experiments and GPT-2/Mamba editing experiments, including accuracy measurements, representation analyses, and city–country results.

after.justification: V3 retains the original synthetic and city–country results and reports revised Llama/Mamba calendar-editing experiments and additional layer-wise analyses.

M1.justification: The proposed synthetic data generator, Transformer training, shattering measure, and visualization procedure remain unchanged. Switching existing editing algorithms in the calendar experiments changes the evaluated interventions and protocol, without introducing a new proposed method component.

E1.justification: Synthetic graph, calendar-month, and city–country task coverage is retained. V3 explicitly evaluates MMLU-Redux, whereas v2 identifies its evaluation only as a reasoning task from Gu et al. (2024). The earlier test is insufficiently specified to establish how represented data or task coverage changed.

E2.justification: MEMIT replaces ROME within the pretrained-model calendar experiments. The synthetic comparison set remains ROME, MEMIT, AlphaEdit, and PMET in Tables 3–4; ROME also remains in the city–country experiment. Thus comparator membership changes locally, rather than MEMIT being newly evaluated throughout the paper.

E3.justification: Section 4.5 substantially revises the calendar protocol: GPT-2 is replaced by Llama 3 8B Instruct, and ROME edits at distances 1–5 give way to MEMIT at distances 1–3. V3 specifies 36 edits per distance, sequential batches of four, consistent ordering, and prompts using offsets eight, nine, and ten. It specifies MMLU-Redux evaluation through ZeroEval and applies the revised editing protocol to Mamba.

E4.justification: New Appendix G.2 compares representations across Llama layers 17–21 and Mamba layers 36–40, supporting extraction at layers 19 and 38. Existing synthetic layer/relation diagnostics, edit-distance analyses, and city–country case studies are retained after relocation.

E5.justification: Existing averaging across edits and contexts and the r² analysis are retained. V3 adds no reported seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical-testing procedures; the revised calendar figures continue to report point results without uncertainty.

E6.justification: GPT-2/ROME calendar results are replaced by Llama/MEMIT reasoning and representation results in v3 Figure 7. Mamba's shattering values change from 0.275, 0.193, 0.190, 0.360, 0.711 at distances 1–5 to 1.226, 1.365, 1.466 at distances 1–3 in v3 Figure 15. These are replacement results under different editing conditions. Layer-wise results are added; Tables 1–4 and the city–country results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The knowledge-graph and composition definitions, Hypothesis 3.3, and shattering metric in Equation 1 remain unchanged. Appendix D.2 adds an explanatory summary of the existing MEMIT update, without new mathematical reasoning, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the synthetic framework, representation shattering as a mechanistic hypothesis, its relationship to edit distance, and evidence of applicability to pretrained language models. Replacing GPT-2 with Llama in the headline experimental examples updates supporting evidence without changing these claims.

C2.justification: V3 removes v2's speculation that Mamba's fluctuating shattering reflects greater model complexity. It adds a rationale for sequential batched editing and explicitly states that Mamba was not evaluated on MMLU-Redux because it was not instruction-tuned. The broader synthetic-to-naturalistic limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D.2 adds MEMIT documentation and identifies public implementations with default hyperparameters. Appendix G.2 specifies representation extraction at the last token, using Llama layer 19 and Mamba layer 38. The city–country model is clarified as GPT-2 XL. The existing synthetic implementation details and promise of a future code release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds references for Llama 3, MMLU-Redux, ZeroEval, Gupta et al.'s unified editing framework, and Yoon et al.'s batch-size study, while removing Radford et al. (2019). Prior work now explicitly motivates sequential editing, but the broader related-work positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Section 4.5 and the Mamba discussion are rewritten locally. The appendices separate synthetic experiments into F and naturalistic experiments into G, move alternative-method comparisons earlier, and expand the editing-method primer. Copyediting, cross-reference corrections, and an affiliation update accompany these changes; the main narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: V2's separate GPT-2 accuracy bars and manifold figure are replaced by a combined Llama accuracy-change curve and manifold display. The Mamba display is replaced, two layer-comparison figures are added, and retained appendix figures and tables are rearranged. The remaining graphical content and table structures are preserved.

improvement.justification: V3 improves experimental transparency through its explicit editing schedule, ordering controls, named evaluation framework, and layer-selection diagnostics. These make the naturalistic evidence easier to assess. The revised experiments replace earlier evidence under different conditions, and the new accuracy plot omits the absolute unedited score, limiting interpretation. The documentation and diagnostic gains nevertheless support a limited overall improvement.
